what_this_is: The pin record of the grib2 adapter: the documents its format is read from, cited by URL and NOT carried (HTML pages and a WMO publication, DECISIONS U-08), with no digest because the design record holds no copy of them; the code-table rows the adapter states words or units for and the file each was read from; the GDAL build that wrote seven of the fixtures; the licence reading behind the adapter's class; and how the synthetic fixture set is built. No node here pairs a `local_path` with a `sha256`: nothing is pinned as a held document.

cited.document: NCEP WMO GRIB2 Documentation, version 37.0.0, 2026-06-01: the index and the section, code-table and template pages under grib2_doc/
cited.read_for: Section 0 (the sixteen octets and the eight-octet total length), Section 1 (octets 12-21: the reference time's significance, the reference time, the production status and the type of processed data), Section 6 (the bitmap indicator, Note 1), Code Tables 1.2, 4.4, 4.10, 5.0, 5.5 and 6.0, Grid Definition Templates 3.0 and 3.30 (Note 1: units of 10^-6 degree and 10^-3 m), Product Definition Templates 4.0 and 4.8 (Note 2: the reference time and the forecast time define the start of the overall interval) and Data Representation Templates 5.3 and 5.41 (octet 20, the PNG bit depth; Note 3, width Ni and height Nj), as research-grib2 F02-F07 and gap-grib2-wire-facts F01 quote them
cited.standing: The index states that nothing in these pages should be considered official and sends a reader to the WMO for the official standard (gap-pin-gate F8); the adapter is read against them because the WMO text below was not obtainable by automation.

cited.document: WMO-No. 306, Manual on Codes, Volume I.2, Part B, FM 92 GRIB edition 2
cited.edition: 2025 edition, amendments FT2025-1 to FT2026-2 as the WMO community page lists them (read 2026-10-14)
cited.standing: Cited by reference, never carried and not a cite-not-carry record (gap-pin-gate F4: the class is defined for bytes that may not lawfully be held, and WMO's obstacle is a script-rendered page and a no-redistribution posture every pinned standard here shares). The licence class of the publication is the maintainer's to confirm at the 3.6.0 release (DECISIONS L-10, L-30).

digest: not stated for any page or for the WMO publication: the design record holds no copy of them (research-grib2 read the NCEP pages on 2026-10-14 and saved none; the WMO library page answered with a human-verification slider), so no SHA-256 was measured and none is claimed. Nothing was fetched for this record (DECISIONS L-06); the 3.6.0 readiness list carries the reading for the maintainer.

tables_read_by_row.why: A GRIB2 message states a parameter, a surface and an earth shape as codes. The adapter states words or a unit only for the rows below, each read from the file named; every other code is carried as the code alone (the Limitation `tables-read-by-row`).

gdal_tables.build: GDAL 3.13.3 "Iowa City", released 2026/08/13, the Homebrew bottle 3.13.3_2
gdal_tables.generated_from: each file's own header: generated by frmts/grib/degrib/merge_degrib_and_wmo_tables.py from tables at https://github.com/wmo-im/GRIB2/commit/a9c4acce568f45e3efc183cfa0931a6fb89dc073

files.keyed_by: NCEP's centre 7 and subcentre 0, as the HRRR and RAP messages' Section 1 states them (gap-grib2-wire-facts F01); this file carries no generation header of its own, and CFRZR's unit column states its codes' meanings, so the adapter names CFRZR and states no unit for it

gdal_tables.measured: the SHA-256 with shasum -a 256 and the size from the file system, on 2026-10-17, on the machine that wrote the fixtures; the rows of grib2_table_4_2_0_0, grib2_table_4_2_0_3 and grib2_table_4_2_local_NCEP were added in R5's fix round on the same day, for the HRRR and RAP parameters the design record names (gap-grib2-wire-facts F01)

local_row.document: NSSL, Operational MRMS GRIB2 Tables, 'This information is current for MRMS Version 12.2'
local_row.row: 209 | 6 | 37 | MultiSensor_QPE_01H_Pass2 | 60-min | mm | Missing -1 | No Coverage -3 | Multi-sensor accumulation 1-hour (1-hour latency), originating centre 161, subcentre 0
local_row.read_from: research-grib2 F04, which quotes the row as read in a browser on 2026-10-14

tables_read_by_row.earth_shapes: Code Table 3.2's spheres 0 (radius 6,367,470 m) and 6 (radius 6,371,229 m) are written into the adapter from the table as its author knows it; the design record quotes neither radius, so the two figures are an open reading for the maintainer (reports/R5-build.md, section 7). Shape 1 states its radius in the message and needs no table; the fixtures use shape 1.

licence.reading: The NCEP GRIB2 documentation is a US Government agency's public page (research-grib2 F02), the repository's PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT class; NOAA's data terms (NODD: open to the public, attribution requested; NWS: public domain unless annotated otherwise, research-grib2 F10) are about the data, which never enters this tree. The WMO publication's class is the maintainer's (DECISIONS L-30).
licence.not_a_grant: This record states no permission. It records which class the adapter declares and why, and a later reading is a later record beside this one.

data_posture: No message from any NOAA file — not a message, not a byte range, not a value — enters this tree: the fixtures are synthetic (CONTRIBUTING.md, Synthetic fixtures only). The design record's byte ranges of real messages (work/gap-grib2-wire-facts/raw/) are facts only and were not used as a fixture or a template.
fixtures_are_synthetic: Every payload under fixtures/grib2/ and its malformed/ directory is built by spec/build_fixtures.py from literals in that script, written on 2026-10-17 for this adapter: seven by GDAL from an ASCII grid of literals, six and every malformed payload by the script's own encoder. Every grid lies in the Baltic rectangle and every reference time is 2026-04-29T06:00:00Z. Centre and parameter codes are table codes chosen to exercise the adapter (centre 161 with discipline 209 because the local row above is keyed by them), not a claim about who wrote a message.

builder.check: python -I -B spec/build_fixtures.py --check (prints which GDAL reading it took, then CURRENT, exits 0, writes nothing); with --require-gdal it passes only when GDAL 3.13.3 re-wrote the seven tool-written messages
builder.gdal_reading: GDAL 3.13.3 "Iowa City", released 2026/08/13 (gdal_translate --version), GDAL_DATA /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gdal/3.13.3_2/share/gdal, run with GDAL_PAM_ENABLED=NO from a temporary directory with relative file names: two runs on 2026-10-17 wrote the same octets, whose SHA-256 the script's GDAL_DIGESTS records. A different GDAL build that writes other octets is a new reading of this record, not a defect (DECISIONS U-11: the maintainer re-runs --check --require-gdal on the named build before each release and records the reading here).
builder.pure_python: The six hand-written messages and every malformed payload depend on no library version: the PNG is written with a stored zlib stream the script assembles, its CRCs with zlib.crc32, and every twin is json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) of the script's literals.
